name: Cascade Liquidity Strategy
rootCause: Cascade, a perpetual contract platform backed by institutions including Polychain, was attacked on Arbitrum through its pre-launch locked CLS vault (First Wave invite-only deposits). The attacker accumulated long positions in a low-liquidity market to hedge against CLS short positions, artificially manipulated the mark price upward, triggering large-scale liquidations of CLS short positions. After profiting from the attack, the attacker immediately withdrew approximately $1.34 million USDC. The project team paused trading and withdrawals, and the funds were largely recovered afterward, with full compensation arranged for affected users.

descriptions.text: Cascade, a perpetual contract platform backed by institutions including Polychain, was attacked on Arbitrum through its pre-launch locked CLS vault (First Wave invite-only deposits). The attacker accumulated long positions in a low-liquidity market to hedge against CLS short positions, artificially manipulated the mark price upward, triggering large-scale liquidations of CLS short positions. After profiting from the attack, the attacker immediately withdrew approximately $1.34 million USDC. The project team paused trading and withdrawals, and the funds were largely recovered afterward, with full compensation arranged for affected users.

Cascade’s CLS vault on Arbitrum was exploited on 15 July 2026. Attackers manipulated mark prices in a thin-liquidity perpetuals market to force liquidation of vault short positions, resulting in losses of around $1.34 million. The stolen USDC was bridged to Solana, swapped to DAI, and deposited on Ethereum to evade freezing. The CLS vault's mark price logic allowed attacker-controlled positions in thin markets to artificially inflate prices, forcing liquidation of vault short positions at manipulated levels. No manipulation-resistant oracle or price-sanity checks were built into the contract, leaving it vulnerable to targeted price moves by attackers.
